# Story 78 — Customer reopens a resolved ticket inside the window (WEB) (Story: CRM-92)

## Prerequisites

- **TICKETS-11-API (CRM-91)** shipped: the ticket-read endpoint returns whether the resolved ticket is still reopenable (the window is the API's fact), and a customer-visible reply on a resolved ticket inside the window reopens it. Coordinate with the API author on the exact field name and the error `code` returned when a reply arrives after the window (this plan assumes a boolean flag on the ticket read payload and reuses the shared error-code sentence — the executor **must confirm both** by reading the API's response shape before touching the screen).
- **PORTAL-2-WEB / PORTAL-3-WEB (CRM-122 / CRM-123)** — the customer's ticket-reading screen (`web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.tsx`) already exists and is the screen this story extends.
- **CONVERSATION-3-WEB (CRM-90)** — the customer reply control on the portal ticket screen. This story does not build the reply control from scratch; it decides when the customer sees it on a *resolved* ticket, and the copy that surrounds it.

## Story Goal

On the customer's portal ticket screen (`web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.tsx`) a resolved ticket that is **still inside the reopen window** shows the reply control together with a short sentence explaining that sending a reply will reopen the ticket. A resolved ticket **outside the window** shows neither the reply control nor a reopen action — it shows a short sentence that says the ticket is closed and cannot be reopened here. Every string is added to both `en.ts` and `ar.ts` in the same edit.

**Not in scope:**

- Any `api/` change — owned by **TICKETS-11-API (CRM-91)**.
- Desk-side reopen controls — this story does not touch `pages/tickets/`.
- Timers / auto-close after the window — **TICKETS-14-API**.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** a resolved ticket on the customer portal has no reopen affordance and, if the customer does reply, the API's refusal is surfaced through the shared error map.
- **New behaviour (this story):**
  - Inside the window → the reply control is shown, and above (or beside) it a sentence tells the customer that sending a reply will reopen the ticket.
  - Outside the window → no reply control on a resolved ticket; a short sentence says the ticket is closed and cannot be reopened here. There is no button to press that will be refused.
  - The window is decided by the API: the ticket-read payload carries the flag; the client does not compute it from `updated_at`.

## Implementation tasks

### 1 — Surface the API's window flag on the customer ticket type

**File:** `web/src/pages/portal/useCustomerTicket.ts`

- Add the reopen-window field to the ticket type this hook returns. Name and type must match what **TICKETS-11-API (CRM-91)** actually returns — read the API's response shape from `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js` / `tickets.repository.js` and mirror the field name exactly (a plausible name is `canReopen: boolean`, but do not invent — verify).
- Do **not** compute the window from `resolvedAt` / `updatedAt` on the client. If the API does not carry the flag, stop and coordinate with CRM-91's owner; do not proceed.
- Keep the hook's four-state shape from `useRequest`; do not change its call signature.

### 2 — Render the reopen affordance on `PortalTicketPage`

**File:** `web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.tsx`

- Where the reply control is rendered for an *open* ticket today, extend the condition so that on a **resolved** ticket the control is shown **only when** the API's window flag is truthy.
- Immediately above (or beside) the reply control on a resolved+in-window ticket, render a short sentence from `t.portal.ticket.replyReopens` (see §4 for the exact keys) explaining that sending a reply will reopen the ticket.
- On a resolved ticket where the flag is falsy, render a single sentence from `t.portal.ticket.closedNoReopen` and **do not** render the reply control. This is the "do not offer an action that will be refused" rule already followed by the customer screen's grant-sign-in section.
- All copy comes from `t.*`; no string literals in JSX, no bare separators (`" · "`, `" — "`) between tags.
- Any value interpolated into a translated sentence (e.g. a ticket number in the closed sentence) must be wrapped with U+2068 / U+2069 following the pattern in `pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts`.
- No `required`, `pattern`, `minLength`, `maxLength` on any new form control. The API owns the rules.

### 3 — Handle the "window elapsed" refusal from the reply submit

**File:** `web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.tsx` (or the reply hook it uses, see grep in Context §14)

- When the customer's reply on a resolved-but-just-elapsed ticket is refused by the API (race between page load and submit), read **the shared sentence** for that error code in `t.errors[code]` first (see `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts`). If the shared sentence is wrong for a customer on the portal (it likely says something desk-oriented), add a screen-local sentence under `t.portal.ticket.errors.<code>` and prefer it. Otherwise fall back to the shared map.
- After a successful reply that reopened the ticket, the existing reply success path already refetches the thread; no new state is invented.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Ticket loads inside the window, customer submits after it closes.** API returns the refusal code. Behaviour: surface the sentence chosen in §3; do not hide the reply control mid-flow; leave the customer with something they can read. Enforced in `PortalTicketPage.tsx` error branch of the reply request.
- **Ticket is `open` (not resolved).** The flag is irrelevant; existing reply behaviour is unchanged. Enforced by the condition in §2 being scoped to `status === "resolved"`.
- **Ticket is `resolved` and API omits the window flag (older payload / partial rollout).** Treat as *outside the window* (safer default). Enforced in the condition in §2 (`ticket.canReopen === true`, not `!== false`).
- **Arabic RTL layout.** The two new sentences must render correctly under `dir="rtl"`; any interpolated value must be wrapped in U+2068 / U+2069. Verified by rendering the page with `language: "ar"` in a test (see §Test Plan).
- **Customer visits a resolved ticket that is not theirs.** Out of scope for the screen — enforced by the API (`403`), rendered through the existing error path unchanged.
- **`t.errors[code]` says something wrong for the customer.** Recorded in the intake hints; §3 covers this — read the shared sentence before reusing it.
- **The desk-shell `/me` boot in tests.** Portal pages do not render the desk shell, but if a new render path in the new test suite does, use `src/testing/stub-me.ts` (L-30 for fresh `Response` per fetch stub still applies).

All new tests are Vitest + Testing Library, matching the shape of the existing `web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.test.tsx`.

1. **`web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.test.tsx` — add:**
   1. *Resolved + inside window → reply control and reopen sentence rendered.* Stub the ticket read to return `status: "resolved"` and the window flag truthy. Assert the exact sentence from `t.portal.ticket.replyReopens` is on the screen and the reply textarea is present.
   2. *Resolved + outside window → no reply control, closed sentence rendered.* Stub the window flag falsy. Assert the closed sentence from `t.portal.ticket.closedNoReopen` is on the screen and the reply textarea is **not**.

   5. *Same as (1) with `language: "ar"`* — assert the Arabic sentence is on the screen. Confirms `parity.test.ts` will keep both languages in step.
2. **`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`** — runs unchanged; passes only when the new keys are in both `en.ts` and `ar.ts`.
3. **`web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — runs unchanged; passes only when no literal slipped into JSX.

## Done Criteria

- [x] A resolved ticket inside the window shows the reply control and the reopen sentence.
- [x] Outside the window there is no reply control, and the reason is shown instead.
- [x] A closed ticket is the same: no control, and this screen's own sentence rather than the shared one about a move nobody made.
- [x] The window fact comes from the API's ticket payload (`reopenWindowOpen`), computed with the server's clock. Nothing here counts days.
- [x] The refusal path still works and still reads correctly — the window closing while somebody types, and the desk closing the ticket while they type, are both pinned.
- [x] Both languages (BR-6), including the refusal sentences.
- [x] `cd web && npm test` (282) and `npm run build` green; `cd api && npm test` (458) untouched and green.
- [x] No `api/` file touched.
- [x] Nothing mentions AI assistance.

**This story changed a decision made two stories ago, on purpose.**
`CONVERSATION-3-WEB (CRM-105)` kept the reply box on a ticket whose window had
passed and let the API refuse it, and said so in its plan. TICKETS-11-WEB's
criterion is explicit that a customer is *"not offered an action that will be
refused"*, so the box is now withheld and the reason shown in its place. Three
tests written for the old behaviour were rewritten rather than deleted: two of
them became the race they now describe — the window closing, or the desk
closing the ticket, while somebody is still typing — which is the case where
the refusal path is still reached and still has to read correctly.

The screen decides only whether to draw a box. It reads two facts the API
states, the status and `reopenWindowOpen`, and counts nothing; the API refuses
the write either way.

Three mutations run: offering the box whatever the state fails 3, forgetting
the window and refusing every resolved ticket fails 5, and using one sentence
for both refusals fails 2.
